falsifier: no candidate recovers a must-find on the archive, read by meaning
hypothesis: at least one decision a model makes on the report path could move to code and recover must-finds: the lane a misfiled draft belongs to, the place a led draft cites, or an ID set the output schema leaves open
intervention: three offline readings. (1) Lane: across every archived STRIDE report, 10 drafts were rejected for lane, 7 by the LANES_OF_VERB table (verb not legal in its lane) and 3 by the critic (verb legal). Refiling the 7 to the verb's lane matches a must-find structurally for 3; by meaning 2 (08 ref 18, 13 ref 0), and in both runs another kept draft (08 E-01, 13 S-04) already answers that reference, so refiling adds duplicates and recovers 0. The one critic lane rejection matching a must-find (12 E-01) reads as spoofing by meaning, as the critic ruled. (2) Place: snapping a free draft in the lane to an overlapping candidate lead recovers 0 of the 18 place and unled must-find misses on 6bff717 after the rulings. (3) Schema sets: every not-in check in validation.py either has its enum (Assumption.attribute, Ground and UnknownRef attributes) or tests against IDs the same output declares; the 103 unresolved references over 901 claims in four Baselines are all the fan-in hop bound, none an invented ID
reconsider_when: a sweep shows lane rejections whose finding no other draft states, or the output schema gains a field checked against a computed set
scope: four Baselines and every archived STRIDE report under evals/runs, offline; the meaning reading is one reader's judgement
